toegepas.blok: Hoe brande in ons gemeenskappe begin
toegepas.rede_vinder: A Grade 5 reader can take 'kom ... uit' as 'heat comes out of fuel', the opposite of the intended 'heat reaches fuel'; 'bereik' removes that misreading.
toegepas.fout: 'kom hitte by brandstof uit' can make a reader stumble in a lesson that uses 'uitkom' for energy coming out (uitset), so it can read as heat coming out of fuel
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'bereik hitte 'n brandstof' says the same thing (heat gets to the fuel) with no ambiguity and keeps the same people, action and scope.

laat_vaar.blok: Hoe brande in ons gemeenskappe begin
laat_vaar.voor: kry vuurhoutjies of 'n aansteker in die hande
laat_vaar.na: kry vuurhoutjies of 'n aansteker in hul hande
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: 'In hul hande kry' is the natural possessive form; 'in die hande' reads like an anglicised or clipped construction.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'Iets in die hande kry' is the idiomatic Afrikaans form, since Afrikaans uses the article with body parts, so the proposal is a lateral move built on a mistaken reason.

laat_vaar.na: hoog op 'n plek waar klein kinders
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: 'Hoog op waar' leaves 'op' hanging without a noun; naming 'n plek makes the relative clause attach cleanly.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'hoog op waar klein kinders nie kan bykom nie' is acceptable spoken Afrikaans, and 'hoog op 'n plek' is no smoother, so rewording a fire-prevention rule is not justified.

na_skrywer.rede_vinder: 'Lig gee' is the idiomatic Afrikaans collocation for a lamp; 'lig maak' is wooden.
na_skrywer.fout: 'n Lamp wat lig maak' is wooden next to the natural collocation 'lig gee', and 'lig maak' can also be read as 'make lighter'
na_skrywer.rede_keurder: The fault is real, but this is a glossary definition and a word change beyond spelling or grammar, so the writer has to make it.
na_skrywer.waarom: the reviewer sent it to the writer

laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: In the sense of reaching something, the idiom is 'by iets kom'; 'bykom' on its own means to regain consciousness.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'bykom' does mean to reach or get at in Afrikaans, so 'waar klein kinders nie kan bykom nie' is correct, and 'waar ... daarby' in the proposal is clumsier.

laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: A plug goes 'in' a wall socket; 'by' is the wrong preposition here.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'by een muurprop' covers plugs connected at one socket through adapters, which is how a socket is overloaded; 'in' narrows that to what fits into the socket itself, so the preposition swap is not proved meaning-neutral.

laat_vaar_vorige.blok: Wat om te doen tydens 'n brand
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: 'totdat' is the standard conjunction before a clause; 'tot' is a preposition.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'tot' is an accepted Afrikaans conjunction before a clause ('rol tot die vlamme dood is'), and the sentence is a safety instruction that already reads well.

laat_vaar_vorige.voor: gee vir die hout daardie eerste hitte
laat_vaar_vorige.na: gee die hout daardie eerste hitte
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: With 'gee' the indirect object reads more naturally without 'vir'; 'eerste hitte' stays intact.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'gee vir die hout' is ordinary, natural Afrikaans and marks the indirect object clearly for a Grade 5 reader; dropping 'vir' is a lateral move that puts 'die hout daardie' side by side.
